blocks.text: **The problem.** A phrase is a **palindrome** if, after turning every uppercase letter into lowercase and removing everything that isn't a letter or a digit, it reads the same forwards and backwards. Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome.

blocks.alt: The phrase No lemon, no melon as 18 boxes. The spaces (empty boxes) and the comma are grey: they are skipped. Ignoring them and ignoring case, the letters read n o l e m o n n o m e l o n, the same in both directions.

elements.text: grey: not a letter or digit, so skipped

elements.originalText: n o l e m o n | n o m e l o n

blocks.code:
s = "No lemon, no melon"                ->  true
s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"    ->  true
s = "race a car"                        ->  false   ("raceacar" backwards is "racaecar")
s = " "                                 ->  true    (nothing left: an empty string reads the same)

blocks.text: The idea: compare mirror pairs, skipping the noise

A palindrome's first character equals its last, its second equals its second-to-last, and so on — the two-pointer check. The only twist is the noise: spaces, commas and case. The obvious fix is to clean the string first. The better fix is to let each pointer **skip** the characters that don't count, so no cleaned copy is ever made.
Build the cleaned lowercase string, then check it equals its own reverse.
**Time O(n), space O(n).** Three passes — clean, reverse, compare — and two new strings as long as the input.

Start at both ends. If the left character isn't a letter or digit, step past it; same on the right. When both point at real characters, compare them ignoring case: a mismatch means `false`, a match moves both inwards.

blocks.caption: Grey characters are skipped; each matching pair turns green. Try the one that isn't a palindrome.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(1).** Every step moves at least one pointer, so there are at most n steps, and only two indexes are stored.

blocks.alt: Clean and reverse: O(n) time, O(n) space. Two pointers: O(n) time, O(1) space.

blocks.text: Approach 1 is quick to write and fine to start with; interviewers usually ask next for O(1) space, which is approach 2.

items: **Only punctuation or spaces** — nothing is left, and an empty string counts as a palindrome: `true`.
**Digits** — they count: `"0P"` is `false` because `0` and `p` differ.
**Skipping past each other** — a run of punctuation in the middle must not let a pointer run off the end; the `left < right` check in the loop guards it.
**Valid Palindrome II** — the same check, but one character may be deleted. Next lesson.
**Palindrome Number** — the same idea on the digits of an integer, without converting it to a string: reverse half of the number.
**Palindrome Linked List** — no index from the end, so find the middle with slow/fast pointers and reverse the second half (Linked List course).
